articles.title: GRFNet, PyTorch model for multichannel time-series classification [P]

articles.title: A Repeatable Review Routine for Daily AI Commits
articles.summary:
Quick answer: When AI commits arrive daily, the review has to be a routine, not a fresh negotiation each time. Run the same sequence on every change: scope the diff against the task, read the flagged suspicions in risk order, confirm the related context, verify the changed path with real requests and a flow check, then hand off the confirmed items. A time box keeps it fast, and a fixed checklist keeps the standard from drifting when the team is busy.

articles.title: Reviewing a Large AI-Generated Diff Without Reading Every Line
articles.summary:
Quick answer: When an AI tool produces a diff that spans dozens of files, reading every line in order is the slowest and least reliable way to review it. A better routine reads the diff in risk-ordered passes: first the changed behavior and the flagged suspicions with their code evidence, then the shared modules and the scope of the change, and only then the low-risk formatting. Real requests against the API confirm the behavior the diff only implies. This keeps the review fast without turning it into a rubber stamp.

articles.title: CRM Field Mapping: Decide Who Owns Each Value
articles.summary:
By JC TechLabs

Connected records. Clear ownership.

CRM field mapping is more than pairing two column names. It defines what a value means, which system may change it and what happens when connected records disagree.

A connector can successfully deliver an update that the business should never have accepted. Before connecting a CRM to another application, make those decisions visible.

articles.title: Varlock Releases Bumpy: A File-Based Versioning Alternative to Changesets
articles.summary: Bumpy is an MIT-licensed, TypeScript tool for version management and changelogs in monorepos. It follows the changesets workflow, using markdown bump files, and adds support for workspace and catalog protocols, custom publish commands, and branch-based prereleases. Changesets v3, released in August 2026, closed many earlier gaps, though differences remain. By Daniel Curtis

articles.title: How Grab Improved Mobile App Stability by Safely Handling Surge in AI-Generated Code Changes
articles.summary: The growing adoption of AI coding assistants has accelerated development and increased the volume of code changes per release, bringing more opportunities for defects and crashes, says Grab. To address these challenges, they implemented a layered defense strategy to prevent, detect, and contain crashes throughout the development and release lifecycle. By Sergio De Simone
